issues: The edit adds label_smoothing=0.05 to the cross-entropy inside GPT.forward. The same forward path is used during evaluation: the val_bpb evaluator calls model(x, y, reduction='none') and adds up the per-token losses. So the smoothed loss is what gets turned into bits per byte, and the measured val_bpb is no longer the true cross-entropy. This changes how val_bpb is measured (category 1), and it explains why the harness rejected the run on an integrity flag.

Because the training loss and the eval loss share one code path, any score from this run cannot be compared with the incumbent. Smoothing adds a uniform-target term to the reported per-token loss, so the bpb changes for reasons unrelated to model quality (category 2).

A valid way to test label smoothing: apply it only in the training loop, for example by computing F.cross_entropy(..., label_smoothing=...) on logits in train.py's training step. Alternatively, gate it on self.training, and keep the reduction='none' eval path exactly as it is in the incumbent.
The harness gives no numbers, only an integrity rejection, so z cannot be recomputed and there are no stated gains to check.
